Delete Account and Export Health Data have no action.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the settings screen
sections.what: Brings in the layout pieces, icons, navigation, theme values and shared card and divider components the page needs.
sections.why: Standard setup at the top of a screen file.

sections.name: SettingsScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Switch states and settings groups
sections.what: Keeps the on or off state for six switches and builds the groups: Preferences, Notifications, Security, Privacy and Consent, and Data. Some rows show fixed text such as English (India) and Asia/Kolkata that the user cannot change here.
sections.why: Likely reason: the consent switches start off, which is the cautious default for privacy choices.
sections.watch_out: The switches only change memory on this screen. Nothing is stored on the device or server, so they reset when the app restarts.

sections.name: SettingsScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Drawing the groups and rows
sections.what: Draws the header and each group as a card. Each row shows an icon, a label, an optional subtitle, and either a switch or an arrow. Export Health Data and Delete Account are shown as rows but do nothing when tapped.
sections.why: Likely reason: one repeated layout means new rows only need a new entry in the groups list.
sections.watch_out: Rows use their label as their unique key, so two rows with the same label could confuse the list.

sections.name: SettingsScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Styles for the settings screen
sections.what: Defines the look of the header, back button, section titles, row spacing and icon boxes.
sections.why: Keeps styling apart from the layout code, so it is easier to change.
sections.watch_out: Several sizes here are plain numbers instead of the shared text sizes, so this screen may not match others exactly.

summary: The Settings page: a list of switches and rows covering preferences, notifications, security, privacy consent and data.
purpose: Lets the user look at and change app options, including privacy consent choices.
why: Likely reason: keeps all options in one place. Reason not stated in the code beyond that.
how: Keeps the on or off state of each switch, builds a list of groups and rows, and draws each group as a card with dividers between rows. The back button returns to the previous screen.
inputs: The user's taps on switches and rows. No data is loaded from the server.
outputs: Changed switch positions on screen only. Nothing is saved and no server calls are made.
risks: Switches look as if they save, but they do not. Export Health Data and Delete Account do nothing when tapped. Consent switches look like a real privacy record but are not sent anywhere. Language and timezone are fixed text.
debug: If a switch resets after leaving the screen, that is current behavior: nothing is saved. To find or add a row, look at the groups list in this file. If a row does nothing, check whether it has an action attached; export and delete have none yet.
